setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): Garcia plays smoking leads throughout the song; The jam features an extended, uninhibited Garcia guitar showcase, which the reviewer calls the show's high point [8][9][15]
- **Me And My Uncle** (2 reviews): Recommended as the one tune to hear if short on time; Garcia's picking on this song is singled out as good [13][14]
- **Cumberland Blues//** (1 other source): The recording cuts off during the last verse [1]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Described as a classic version of the song [4]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-12-23.132343.sbd.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 75 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd70-12-23.sbd.unknown.31608.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 44 min; rated 4.75/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the mix and recording great, a fine example of the 1970 sound; Reviewer says the recording sounds fantastic [8][15]
- **gd70-12-23.sbd.vernon.10376.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 24 min; rated 4/5 by 14 [3]. Said about its sound: Sound quality and vocals are very good; Lesh drives every song, though Garcia sits low on Hard To Handle; Sound is very good for the era [4][13]

## Around the show

- Attendee says it was billed as the Acoustic Grateful Dead, with only about 100 people in the hall [11]
- During New Riders' set a vat of electric apple cider was wheeled out; then the full electric Dead played, followed by Electric Hot Tuna [11]
- Attendee recalls the Dead playing roughly a two-hour set [11]
- Benefit for the Montessori School and Bear, with Hot Tuna playing acoustic, New Riders of the Purple Sage, and Lizard also listed [1]
- At the end Phil wishes everyone a Merry Christmas; Jerry thanks the crowd for helping bail out Bear [2]
- The show was billed as a Montessori School benefit featuring the Acoustic Dead with Hot Tuna and New Riders of the Purple Sage [2]
- Benefit for the Montessori School and Bear; New Riders played a set, and DeadBase IX lists Hot Tuna and Lizard [3]
- The recording is incomplete; the reviewer wishes the whole show were available [4]
- Bear's cassettes list a different setlist from DeadBase: Bobby McGee through Uncle John's Band, with Good Lovin' split around Drums [5]
- Reviewer finds more inspired performances of these songs elsewhere, calling the show mediocre for 1970 [13]
- This is the complete set; the four-song excerpt from Hard To Handle to Cold Rain and Snow is actually from 12/17/70 [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-12-23.132343.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (d1t01 - d1t06) SBD -> Master Reel -> CD -> FLAC(d1t07 - d1t11) SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Cassette -> FLAC [1]. Also: Pitch correction was done with help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd70-12-23.sbd.unknown.31608.sbeok.flacf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd70-12-23.sbd.vernon.10376.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard Partial [3]. Also: Rob Eaton's transcript describes a 45-minute vault soundboard reel: 7-inch master at 7.5ips, to Technics first-generation reel, and onward [3]
